notes: THE SUIT SERVICES (Dean, 2026-08-10). Each suit owns one Service, printed as its FOURTH starter and in its tableau from setup. There is no Hiring Fair, no hire fee, no Working Week track, no expiry and no meeple: the Service belongs to the suit, permanently, and the only Services on the table are the ones the seats' suits brought.

The Service is an ordinary building in every respect that matters: it has a threshold, it clogs when full, and its owner clears it with a Harvest action. What is NOT ordinary is who may put a card on it - a rival may, as their bonus slot, and that is the only building in the game besides the Notice Board that a rival may touch.

TWO WAYS IN, and the asymmetry is the whole rule. A RIVAL places 1 card from hand onto the Service (advancing its threshold), takes the Service's action, and that is the whole transaction. The OWNER pays ownerActivationCost to the bank, takes the action, and places NOTHING - so an owner never clogs their own Service and never earns from their own farm.

THE CARD IS THE PAYMENT (Dean, 2026-08-10). visitWage is 0: a rival's use pays the owner nothing but the card that lands on their Service. That card rides into their barn on the next harvest as exactly the mixed colour the island demands of them, so being useful is paid in FREIGHT rather than in coin - 'your junk is their treasure', now the only thing a visit gives. The GBP 1 wage the first build shipped was measured and removed; keep the wage at 0 unless a table says the owner feels unrewarded, and reach for overlays/service-wage-one.overlay.json before inventing anything new.

So the bonus slot is one option per currency: a CARD buys a neighbour's action, a CARD buys GBP 1 at their Notice Board, a COIN buys your own action, GBP 3 buys a card at market. The Notice Board is now the only cross-table faucet in the game, which makes it the thing to watch if coins dry up.

Every Service performs an ENHANCED version of its action, not the plain one. The reason is the self-cancellation law generalised: a visitor pays a card, so an action that also SPENDS cards (sow, build) is priced in the currency it consumes and is worthless to buy unless it over-delivers. Help is therefore inversely proportional to how card-hungry the action is - draw and sow and build carry real enhancements, harvest and deliver carry small ones.

THE SELF-CANCELLATION LAW, restated for Draw 2 (2026-08-09). The Draw Service is a plain Draw 2 - see 2, keep 2. The law it obeys is about VOLUME, not selection: a buyer pays 1 card and gains 2, so it is card-POSITIVE and worth buying. If anybody ever tidies this to Draw 1 the Service becomes exactly worthless to visit overnight, which is the trap the old printed exception (Draw 3, keep 2) was written to avoid. The selection was measured and found to be doing nothing - see the arms - so it went, and the only player who now gets selection on it is the Orchard seat, through their Farmstead modifier. That is a better statement of "this is the draw suit" than everyone getting best-2-of-3.

Sow takes its card from the TOP OF A DECK, not from the visitor's hand. A hand-sow would cost the buyer two cards (the fee and the sown card) for one threshold step, which is the Draw problem in reverse; drawing the sown card off a deck fixes it and is the better theme besides - the pollinator carries something in from elsewhere.

Build waives the crop requirements rather than discounting the price. A discount of 2 was measured against total throughput and rejected: it saves a Dairy player roughly as many cards over a game as base Draw supplies, and it stacks with the Dairy Farmstead's own-crop discount. Waiving the match costs the card economy nothing and unblocks the thing that actually stops a build, which is holding the wrong colours.

THE BUILDER'S YARD GAINS A DISCOUNT OF 1 (Dean, 2026-08-10, the Dairy rebuild). It now waives the crop requirements AND takes a card off the price, which exactly refunds the card the visitor placed on it. This KNOWINGLY REVERSES the paragraph above and outstanding-rule-changes.md section 5, which chose the waiver alone on owner-side grounds. The owner-side argument is not refuted, it is outweighed by the visitor side: Build took 5% of all rival Service uses and 2.8 rival cards a game, both last in the game, and the traffic ranking is the win ranking in exact order. The Dairy Farmstead no longer substitutes for its own seat (it diverts a spent card to the barn instead), so the stacking this paragraph warned about no longer exists - a Dairy seat matches crops like everybody else, which is what makes its own Service worth visiting. Re-measure before keeping it if the Service-suit weld is ever broken.

Harvest and Deliver share one primitive, `handToBarn`: an optional hand card into your own barn. On Harvest it lands after (a junk sink, worth a real half-crate since the wild substitution). On Deliver it lands before, which is exactly 'you may pay up to 1 card of the cost from your hand' with no second code path. Both are OPTIONAL, so neither can ever be a downside.

linkedSuit is now ownership, not flavour: the seat playing that suit owns that Service and nobody else can. A Service whose suit is not at the table is simply not in the game, and that is a feature - the table's menu of buyable actions is decided by which suits were chosen.
RULING (carried over, unchanged): suit powers apply to actions performed by a Service. It is your action, done on someone else's premises.
unresolved: THE THRESHOLD IS THE BALANCE LEVER, and it is 2 (Dean, 2026-08-09). It is not a flavour number and it must not be raised without re-running the suite. A Service that fills in two cards clogs often, and a clogged Service refuses visits, so the threshold throttles the FREIGHT a popular farm collects - which is the only thing ever measured to touch the suit balance. Monotone and self-targeting across three paired n=1580 arms: at t=4 Orchard won 80.8%, at t=3 62.8%, at t=2 42.0% against an even share of 36.4%. A farm taking 22 rival cards a game feels it; one taking 2.8 does not. Never played at a table.

visitWage is RULED at 0 (Dean, 2026-08-10): the card is reward enough. overlays/service-wage-one.overlay.json restores the GBP 1 as the paired control, so the question can always be re-read as a delta.

A10 The Cross-Pollinator printed 'HIRE a Hired Worker, paying GBP 1 less' and hiring no longer exists. Retexted in the handler to 'Your Service costs GBP 1 less to activate', which the sheet has not caught up with.
